title: Holding More Than One Plan in the Mountain Dining Plans Range on One Household Account
content:
A household account may carry more than one plan in the Mountain Dining Plans range at once, up to 2 plans, counting plans that stand in the enrolled, active, suspended and exhausted states. Two live plans of the same kind are never opened for the same named holder in the same season; where a household wants more spending power they load the plan they hold rather than open a second, because two balances on one holder cannot both be presented at a till. Plans that have reached expired, cancelled or closed no longer count against the account. Corporate accounts take only the plans this charter sells to them, and a household plan is never converted into a corporate one.

## What is compared, and on whose word

The comparison that decides whether a plan of the same kind is already held is made before the plan is opened and on the collective's own records, not on the household's recollection. The records compared are the household account the plan would be opened on, the name the plan is registered to and the season the plan is sold for; a plan already standing against that same account, that same name and that same season, and naming the same plan, is a plan of the same kind. Only records standing in the enrolled, active, suspended or exhausted state enter the comparison.

## Points of judgement

**Counting towards the limit.** An account showing one plan in the active state, one in the exhausted state and one in the cancelled state carries two plans that count and one that does not, and so stands at the limit of 2.

**The same holder in the same season.** Where the account already shows a plan of that kind in the active state registered to that name for that season, a second of the same kind is not opened for that name; the plan already held takes the further money instead.

**Two names in one household.** Two plans registered to two different named holders on the same account stand as two plans against the limit of 2, and neither is a plan of the same kind for the same named holder.

**A corporate account.** A corporate account takes only those plans in the range the charter sells to corporate accounts. A plan already held by a household is not turned into a corporate one.
